editorial:
Imagine having to pick up all the pieces of your life while your older brother gets to just walk back in and act like nothing happened. That is exactly what you get with this story. You follow Michael, a guy who is totally burnt out from working three jobs just to keep his younger brother Tommy and Tommy's girlfriend safe. When Sandy Glass gets out of prison after eight years, it throws a huge wrench in everything. While Tommy thinks Sandy is some kind of hero, you can feel the anger and stress building up inside Michael. It is a raw look at a family that is falling apart and the kind of anger that grows when one person does all the work while another just causes trouble.

The acting feels very real, and the tension between the brothers keeps you glued to the screen. You will likely find yourself rooting for Michael, but the movie does a great job showing how complicated family ties are. Some parts move a bit slow, but the emotional payoff is worth it. If you are in the mood for a heavy family drama, you should definitely check it out. Since it is an indie gem, your best bet is renting it on Apple TV for a quick watch or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you love owning high-quality discs.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a heartbreaking realization that Sandy cannot truly change his ways. After a final big fight where all the family secrets come out, Sandy realizes he has destroyed his relationship with Michael forever. He eventually leaves again to avoid ruining Tommy's life too. It ends on a sad but hopeful note, showing Michael finally letting go of the burden and finding peace without his brother around.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves grounded stories about family conflict and redemption.
